question.problem:
The equation of the parabola $y=5{x}^{2}-10x+15$ in vertex form is

$y=$
{{field-1}}$(x\,-$
{{field-2}}$)^{2}+$
{{field-3}}.
question.worked_solution:
To express the equation of the parabola in vertex form, we need to complete the square. 

First, we take out a factor of $5$ from the entire expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}^{2}-10x+15 & =5({x}^{2}-2x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we complete the square for the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x+3 & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 1\cdot x+3 & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 1\cdot x+{1}^{2}-{1}^{2}+3 & = \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 1\cdot x+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+3 & = \\ (x-1)^{2}-{1}^{2}+3 & = \\ (x-1)^{2}-1+3 & = \\ (x-1)^{2}+2 & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute this result back into our original expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}5({x}^{2}-2x+3) & = \\ 5((x-1)^{2}+2) & = \\ 5(x-1)^{2}+10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, expressed in vertex form, the equation of the parabola is $y=5(x-1)^{2}+10.$
